newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH INSURERS STILL NEED LARGER CAPITAL - OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH INSURERS STILL NEED LARGER CAPITAL - OFFICIAL.

text.p: Polish insurers are improving their financial standing, but they are still weak as their premiums growth is not followed by sufficient capital increase, the head of an insurance supervising body said.

The president of the State Insurance Supervision Office (PUNU) said the 1997 premium growth in Poland was seen at six percent in real terms but insurers needed a quick 50-percent increase in their capital to meet safety requirements.

"The whole sector is making small steps, I hope the firms would increase their capitals, there are foreign firms interested (in the sector), but the main thing is to increase firms' capitals," Danuta Walcerz told a news conference.
PUNU saw the overall insurance sector premium growth to 9.9 billion zlotys in 1997 from 8.2 billion last year.

Walcerz said the whole insurance sector was growing slowly and its share in the country's gross domestic product was still very low at 2.3 percent, compared with the average 6.9 percent in the European Union countries.
Walcerz said the life insurance sector had better capital and solvency margins and was set to grow quicker than the non-life sector in the next few years.
"The dynamics of growth in the life insurance sector is likely to be higher than in the non-life (sector) but the non-life is also likely to grow along with the country's economic growth," she said.
Poland's gross domestic product is forecast to remain flat at 5.5 percent this year, compared with 1996.
Five insurance companies have gone bankrupt in the last few years in Poland due to low capitals and wrongly calculated premiums, mainly in car insurances.
Some analysts expect the situation to deteriorate in 1999 when foreign insurance firms would gain unlimited access to the Polish market.
